payload.roles:
- THE OWNER — rules the project, adjudicates gates, and is away for most of a run. Reads chat and the board, not evidence JSON. Every id an agent leaves unexpanded is invisible to them.
- THE WALKING AGENT — runs an iteration through the machine. The tool surface's primary user; the one who writes a script when a tool refuses to give what it plainly should.
- THE PARALLEL AGENT — a second walking agent on a different iteration at the same time. Does not exist yet in practice, and is the reason half of this iteration's hard constraints exist: a per-worktree engine, an ambiguous root, an unsynchronised trunk all break only when this role shows up.
- THE REVIEWING AGENT — the same agent wearing the gate's hat: verify, validate, red team, verdict. Distinguished from the walking agent deliberately, because the failure mode is exactly the two collapsing into one.
- THE FUTURE READER — whoever reads this record months out, including the agent that reopens it. Depends entirely on history being superseded rather than erased, and on refusals naming the fact rather than the count.
- THE ENGINE ITSELF — not a person, but it holds a stake and must be named: it is the shared judge. If it differs per iteration, two gates stop meaning one thing.
payload.tensions:
T1 — THE WALKING AGENT vs THE REVIEWING AGENT. The strongest tension in the iteration, and the one with the most evidence. The walking agent wants the gate to pass; the reviewing agent's job is to try to make it fail. Collapsed into one actor with no form asking for the second, the first wins every time — which is exactly what happened: four review rounds, required since meth-gate-review was written, filled zero times in this project's entire history, while gates went green. The resolution is structural, not a matter of diligence: the compiler injects the rounds so the form itself refuses. Proven by my own failure to fill them TWO GATES AFTER BUILDING THE INJECTION — which is the strongest possible evidence that the defect is systemic and not carelessness, since it survived the author's full attention.

T2 — THE WALKING AGENT vs THE PARALLEL AGENT. The walking agent wants its engine changes live NOW, in its own tree. The parallel agent needs the judge to be the same for both. Sourcing the engine child from the open worktree serves the first and destroys the second. Resolved by engine promotion: engine changes land on TRUNK early under their own discipline (trunk current first, whole suite green IN TRUNK, engine files only, all-or-nothing), while everything else stays isolated. The honest cost is stated rather than hidden: engine code reaches trunk before its own gates have reviewed it, and the suite is the guard.

T3 — THE OWNER vs THE WALKING AGENT, over precision. The agent's ids are precise and the owner cannot see any of them. 'R3', 'N2', 'G5' read as rigour while carrying nothing to the only person who adjudicates. The owner said so directly. Resolved by a voice rule (expand in the same message), and the deeper resolution is that the agent should prefer the plain phrase and keep the id only where traceability genuinely needs it.

T4 — THE ENGINE (as judge) vs THE WALKING AGENT (as its builder). An iteration that improves the tool surface cannot use the improvement it just built: the harness cached the tool list at connect and the shim runs trunk's code. This is not a tension to resolve so much as a cost to declare — hence the law that a workaround is legitimate if and only if the gap it worked around is recorded. Six declared workarounds today, each with its RAID entry.

T5 — THE FUTURE READER vs THE WALKING AGENT, over rewrites. The walking agent wants a clean current state; the future reader needs to know what was believed before and why it changed. Resolved in reopen: prior fills are marked SUPERSEDED, never deleted, and a reopened marker records the reason.

T6 — THE OWNER vs THE ENGINE, over dependencies. The owner's own ruling reversed the project's prior stance: 'we overvalued zero dependency', and one-click install is the real constraint. The engine's zero-dependency instinct is not free — it bought a hand-rolled searcher that lost to ripgrep on every axis. Resolved: a dependency is acceptable when it preserves one-click install; vendoring only for a genuinely zero-runtime-dep goal, and credited loudly.
